**How the name is built**

1. `src/click/core.py:Context.__init__` (lines 472–487) computes the prefix for each context.
   - The top-level context uses the explicit `auto_envvar_prefix="APP"`. It is uppercased, and `-` is replaced with `_`, giving `APP`.
   - Each subcommand context has no explicit prefix, so it takes `f"{parent.auto_envvar_prefix}_{self.info_name.upper()}"` (line 478–480). The `-` to `_` replacement then runs on the result.
   - This gives `APP` for `app`, `APP_DB` for `db`, and `APP_DB_MIGRATE` for `migrate`.

2. `src/click/core.py:Option.resolve_envvar_value` (lines 3399–3421) appends the option name to the prefix.
   - It first calls `Parameter.resolve_envvar_value` (line 2616), which checks any explicit `envvar=`.
   - If that finds nothing, and `allow_from_autoenv` is true and `ctx.auto_envvar_prefix` is set, it builds `f"{ctx.auto_envvar_prefix}_{self.name.upper()}"` (line 3415) and reads it with `os.environ.get`.
   - `self.name` is the parameter name `log_level`, so the result is `APP_DB_MIGRATE_LOG_LEVEL`.
   - An empty value is treated as unset, because of the `if rv:` check.

`Option.value_from_envvar` (line 3423) then processes the raw string.
